title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on How People's Courts Shall Handle Applications for Enforcement of Mediation Documents Issued by Arbitration Institutions
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice Concerning How People's Courts Should Handle Applications for Enforcement of Mediation Documents of Arbitration Institutions

Fa (Jing) Fu [1986] No. 26

To the High People's Courts of All Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government, and the Railway Transport High People's Courts:

Recently, some local people's courts have inquired to our court regarding whether mediation documents issued by arbitration institutions may be enforced through application to a people's court. Upon deliberation, it is considered that, in accordance with the provisions of Article 52, Paragraph 3 of the Economic Contract Law, and Article 161, Paragraph 2 and Article 166 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), where one party fails to perform a mediation document of an arbitration institution that has become legally effective, the other party may apply to the people's court with jurisdiction for enforcement. If the people's court receiving the application finds that the mediation document of the arbitration institution is indeed erroneous, it shall not enforce it and shall notify the original arbitration institution.

August 20, 1986
